ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the intersection of the lines $y = -x + m$ and $y = nx + 4n$ ($n \neq 0$) has an x-coordinate of $-3$. What is the solution set for the inequality $-x + m > nx + 4n$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: When $x<-3$, we have $-x+m>nx+4n$, \\
$\therefore$ the solution set for the inequality $-x+m>nx+4n$ with respect to $x$ is $\boxed{x<-3}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the line y=-x+m slopes downward, the line y=nx+4n slopes upward, and the intersection is marked at x=-3. From the text, at the intersection the two formulas are equal, so substituting x=-3 gives 3+m=-3n+4n=n, hence m=n-3. Substitute this into the inequality: -x+n-3>nx+4n.
